<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Leviticus 20:10">Targ. Y. Lev. XX, 10</cite> <he>שינוק ס׳ וכ׳</he> strangulation with a twisted scarf &c. (v.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:2">Snh. VII, 2</cite> quot. in <cite ref="O00264">preced.</cite>); <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 21:15">Targ. Y. Ex. XXI, 15</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 4a:11">Ab. Zar. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>רמו ליה ס׳ וכ׳</he> they twisted a scarf around his neck and tortured him.
Ber. 51ᵃ (expl. עיטוף) פריס ס׳ וכ׳ spread the scarf over his head; a. e.—Esp. turban.

<cite ref="Pesachim 111b:7">Pes. 111ᵇ</cite> <he>סוּדְרֵיה דמר כי וכ׳</he> your turban looks like that of a scholar, yet I am sure you do not know the benediction (on putting it on: <he>עוטר ישראל בתפארה</he>).

<cite ref="Shabbat 77b:11">Sabb. 77ᵇ</cite> (playful etymology) <he>ס̇ו̇ד̇ר̇א̇ ס̇ו̇ד̇ ה׳ ליר̇א̇יו</he> ‘the secret of the Lord is revealed to those that fear him’ (the turban being the scholar’s apparel); a. e.
